name: Cardinal Health
description: Cardinal Health is one of the three big US drug wholesalers; 92 percent of its $254.2 billion FY2026 revenue is pharmaceutical distribution, earning a segment margin of about 1.2 percent. The profit comes disproportionately from smaller businesses: the Other segment (at-Home Solutions, nuclear pharmacies and OptiFreight logistics) is 2.7 percent of revenue but 19 percent of segment profit, and the medical products segment, which manufactures and distributes its own-brand surgical and lab supplies, is the turnaround story with profit up 91 percent. It is highly dependent on one customer: CVS Health was 28 percent of FY2026 revenue.

gics.note: Conventional filing: Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (read 2026-09-30) gives sector Health Care and sub-industry Health Care Distributors; industry group and industry not listed there, left null. SEC SIC 5122.

hq.note: Per Wikipedia List of S&P 500 companies

businessLines.name: Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions
businessLines.how: Buys drugs from manufacturers and sells to pharmacies, hospitals and clinics at a small markup plus service fees (distribution, generics sourcing program, specialty services); revenue is mostly pass-through drug cost and rises with drug prices and volume. CVS Health alone is 28% of company revenue.
businessLines.description: Distribution of branded, generic, specialty and over-the-counter drugs in the US, services to manufacturers and providers for specialty drugs, pharmacy management for hospitals, and management services organisation (MSO) platforms for physician practices (urology via Solaris Health).

revenue.note: FY2025 204,644 (+15%), from branded and specialty drug sales growth from existing and new customers

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2025 204,644 (+15%), from branded and specialty drug sales growth from existing and new customers

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit; FY2025 2,258 (+23%) from branded and specialty products, generics program and MSO acquisitions. Share is of total segment profit $3,748M.

businessLines.name: Global Medical Products and Distribution
businessLines.how: One-time sale of repeat-ordered consumable supplies (gloves, gowns, syringes, lab products), higher margin on own-brand products it makes or sources than on national brands it resells.
businessLines.description: Manufactures, sources and distributes Cardinal Health brand medical, surgical and laboratory products and distributes national-brand products to hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers and clinical labs in the US, Canada, Europe and Asia.

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit; FY2025 135 (+91%) on growth from existing customers; net tariff impact not significant after an IEEPA tariff refund benefit

businessLines.name: Other
businessLines.how: Supplies bought by insurers and patients for chronic conditions delivered to the home (recurring monthly orders), radiopharmaceuticals dispensed per dose by nuclear pharmacies, and per-shipment logistics fees.
businessLines.description: at-Home Solutions (Edgepark and Advanced Diabetes Supply Group supplying patients at home, and a B2B home-medical-equipment supply distributor), Nuclear and Precision Health Solutions (nuclear pharmacies, radiopharmaceuticals, contract manufacturing of Xofigo, Lymphoseek rights) and OptiFreight Logistics.

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit; FY2025 516 (+37%). Small in revenue, 19% of segment profit.

brands.name: Cardinal Health brand products
brands.share: Own-brand medical and surgical products inside Global Medical Products and Distribution ($12,719M revenue, 5.0%); brand-level split not reported

brands.name: Edgepark / Advanced Diabetes Supply Group (ADS)
brands.share: Inside Other segment (2.7% of revenue, 18.9% of segment profit); not separately reported

brands.name: Nuclear and Precision Health Solutions
brands.share: Inside Other segment; not separately reported

brands.name: OptiFreight Logistics
brands.share: Inside Other segment; not separately reported

brands.name: Solaris Health (urology MSO)
brands.share: Acquired in fiscal 2026 for about $1.9B in cash; more than 750 providers across more than 250 locations in 14 states; revenue not separately reported
